Each new poll point is evaluated by the coordination procedure of Algorithm~\ref{alg:operational_planning_degradation} and a point replaces the incumbent only if it improves $F$ by more than the two evaluations’ settling bars (the largest objective step over an evaluation’s last ten cycles) and the measured re

\paragraph{Resolution} The tolerance $\tau$ is set from the value resolution $\delta_R$ the study is to claim: $\tau = \delta_R \mathcal{V}/4$, with $\mathcal{V}$ a reference storage value, so that a ratio of two values --- four evaluations, each in error by at most $\tau$ --- is resolved to $\delta_R$. The rule bounds the stopping error of each evaluation at about $\tau$, not well inside it (Subsection~\ref{subsec:res_certification}); the values used in the case study are given in Section~\ref{sec:case_settings}.
The value of $\alpha$ is given in Section~\ref{sec:case_settings}.

Two comparisons are used throughout Section~\ref{sec:results}. Every candidate plan is compared with the plan without shared storage, $\boldsymbol{x} = \boldsymbol{0}$, under coordinated operation, which isolates the value of the storage investment; and coordinated operation at the plan without storage is compared with two static arrangements of the same system under a no-reverse-flow interface rule (Subsection~\ref{sec:case_settings}), which isolates the value of coordination.

Figure~\ref{fig:res_benchmark} and Table~\ref{tab:res_benchmark} compare coordinated operation with the passive and price-taker arrangements defined in Section~\ref{sec:case_settings}. All three arrangements are evaluated without shared storage, thereby separating the benefit of coordination from that of storage investment. The discounted operational cost is 653{,}873.7~k\euro{} under coordination, compared with 744{,}770.3~k\euro{} for the price-taker arrangement and 895{,}049.9~k\euro{} for the passive arrangement. The two static arrangements therefore cost 13.9\% and 36.9\% more than coordi

The multi-scenario instance combines three market scenarios with three load and renewable-generation scenarios over five representative three-year blocks. The planning search again returned the plan without shared storage, $\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$. As reported in Table~\ref{tab:res_multiscenario}, the reference unit provides an estimated discounted operational value of 236.7~k\euro{} against an investment cost of 318.0~k\euro{}. The resulting shortfall of 81.3~k\euro{} is 4.52 times the reported resolution of 18.0~k\euro{}, supporting the same economic conclusion as the single-scenario

The three planning searches of Algorithm~\ref{alg:shared_ess_planning_mads} made 41 new recourse evaluations in all (14, 20 and 7 against budgets of 20, 20 and 60), each stopped by the production exit of the coordination procedure and compared at the search resolution $\sigma_Q$ of Section~\ref{sec:case_settings}; the evaluations behind the tables of this section are the re-evaluations of the incumbents, their neighbours and the sensitivity cells under the certification rule, on the final code.

In the cycle after a cycle in which every channel passed and every solve succeeded, the TSO and DSO solves are run with the interior-point complementarity tolerance tightened to $10^{-6}$ (the tight tail); the production setting restores each operator's own tolerance otherwise (the tail is a declared option, enabled in every campaign behind the reported tables), and the certifying regime holds the tail on from the cycle after $k_0$.
